description: An agent reviews a pull request. You read the review, and Night Shift posts it on GitHub when you agree.

inputs.name: pr
inputs.label: Pull request
inputs.description: The number or the URL of the pull request.

nodes.label: Review
nodes.prompt:
Review pull request {{pr}} of this repository. Read it with `gh`: its description (`gh pr view {{pr}}`), the linked issue, and the diff (`gh pr diff {{pr}}`). Do not change the code and do not post anything: a person reads your review first.

Look for bugs, missing tests, and changes the description does not explain. Report `approve` when it can merge as it is, else `request-changes`. Put a short `summary` of your verdict in the data, and one entry in `comments` per finding: the file `path`, the `line` in the new version, and the `body`.

outcomes.name: approve
outcomes.description: It can merge as it is.

outcomes.name: request-changes
outcomes.description: The comments must be addressed first.

nodes.label: Post it?

options.name: post
options.description: Post the review on GitHub. On your own pull request, it posts as a comment.

nodes.label: Post the review
nodes.command:
# Templates arrive as environment variables, so the review text is never shell code.
set -e
case "{{review.outcome}}" in
	approve) verdict=--approve ;;
	*) verdict=--request-changes ;;
esac
# GitHub refuses to approve or request changes on your own pull request: comment instead.
author=$(gh pr view "{{pr}}" --json author --jq .author.login)
me=$(gh api user --jq .login)
if [ "$author" = "$me" ]; then
	verdict=--comment
fi
body=$(printf '%s\n\n%s' "{{review.data.summary}}" "{{comments.data.text}}")
gh pr review "{{pr}}" "$verdict" --body "$body"
